source_caption:
"I would just basically put myself through hell. But I don’t do that anymore."

The Oscar-nominated actress Florence Pugh revealed during a interview on The Louis Theroux Podcast that playing Dani Ardor in the Ari Aster-directed horror film Midsommar was so mentally taxing that it resulted in six months of depression. Pugh explained she "put herself through hell" to portray the character's intense grief and trauma, later stating she wouldn't push herself to that level again. 

Midsommar (2019) remains one of the rarest "daylight horror" films in cinema history, trading shadows and jump-scares for the blinding, inescapable sun of a Swedish midsummer festival. Directed by Ari Aster, the story follows a grieving American woman named Dani (Florence Pugh) who accompanies her distant boyfriend, Christian and his friends on a trip to a remote, rural Swedish village for a once-in-90-years Midsummer festival. What begins as an idyllic, sunny retreat quickly devolves into a terrifying, violent, and bizarre series of rituals conducted by a pagan cult known as the Hårga.

source_details.synopsis: Midsommar is a 2019 folk horror film written and directed by Ari Aster. It stars Florence Pugh and Jack Reynor as an American couple who are drawn into a violent cult in rural Sweden. Supporting actors include William Jackson Harper, Vilhelm Blomgren, Ellora Torchia, Archie Madekwe, and Will Poulter. A co-production between the United States and Sweden, Midsommar was initially pitched to Aster as a straightforward slasher film set among Swedish cultists. While elements of the original concept remain in the final product, the finished film focuses on a deteriorating relationship inspired by a difficult breakup experienced by Aster himself.
